title: Do these four more simplifying claims hold up?
description: Four more claims are checked. A plus sign before a bracket changes no sign, a minus sign changes every sign inside, and like terms are then added. The video ends with the chairs and tables that a shop rents out.
teaching_notes: One idea: a plus sign before a bracket changes nothing, a minus sign before it changes every sign inside, and then like terms are added. Watch for students who change only the first sign inside a minus bracket.

video_script.why: A learner sees how the sign before a bracket decides whether the signs inside change.
video_script.substitution: the book's four claims, each checked with the sign before the bracket and then by adding like terms
video_script.anchor: the four claims of the book, each written with its supposed simplified form
video_script.payoff_line: None of these four claims is right, and each is corrected.

final_answer.spoken: three plus six z; x plus five; five y minus six; six p plus three q

maths_rules: real life: the shop pays 40x + 75y for x chairs and y tables and gives back 6x + 10y, so the return is a minus sign before a bracket
video_script.design: The four claims stay on the board; the bracket in each is opened by the sign before it, like terms are added, and the wrong forms are struck out.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four more claims, each an expression with its supposed simplified form

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the four claims are written
marks.claims: each claim is lit one after another
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the four claims

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is the next question in your book. It gives four more claims about simplifying.
<bookmark mark='claims'/>Three of them have a bracket, and one has only letter-numbers added and taken away.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these claims are right?

beats.on_screen: the four claims stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: plus sign before a bracket: no sign changes; minus sign before a bracket: every sign inside changes

marks.plus: a plus sign before a bracket is shown with the signs inside staying the same
marks.minus: a minus sign before a bracket is shown with every sign inside flipping
marks.like: like terms are circled in one colour

narration: <bookmark mark='plus'/>The plus sign before a bracket changes no sign inside it.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>The minus sign before a bracket changes the sign of every term inside it.
<bookmark mark='like'/>After the bracket opens, like terms are added together.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Given, the claim that five minus the bracket two minus six z is three minus six z.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Next, two plus the bracket x plus three is two x minus six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Next, two y plus the bracket three y minus six is minus y plus six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Last, seven p minus p plus five q minus two q is seven p plus three q.

beats.on_screen: To find: which claims are right, and the correct form of the others

marks.find: the words right or wrong, and correct form are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to check each claim, and correct the wrong ones.

marks.flip: the signs inside the bracket flip, and − 6z becomes + 6z
marks.line: 5 − 2 + 6z = 3 + 6z is written, and the claim 3 − 6z is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='flip'/>Step one, the minus sign before the bracket changes both signs inside.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Five minus two plus six z is three plus six z. The claim missed the sign of six z.

marks.same: the bracket opens with its signs unchanged
marks.line: 2 + x + 3 = x + 5 is written, and the claim 2x − 6 is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step two, the plus sign before the bracket changes no sign.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Two plus x plus three is x plus five. The two and the three are added, and x stays alone.

marks.same: the bracket opens with its signs unchanged
marks.line: 2y + 3y − 6 = 5y − 6 is written, and the claim − y + 6 is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, the bracket opens with no change.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Two y plus three y minus six. Two y plus three y is five y, so the form is five y minus six.

marks.pq: the p terms and the q terms are circled in two colours
marks.line: (7 − 1)p + (5 − 2)q = 6p + 3q is written, and the claim 7p + 3q is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='pq'/>Step four, group the p terms and the q terms.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Seven p minus p is seven minus one, times p, which is six p. Five q minus two q is three q. The claim kept seven p.

marks.forms: the four right forms are lit in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>None of these four claims is right, and each is corrected.
<bookmark mark='forms'/>The right forms are three plus six z and x plus five. The others are five y minus six and six p plus three q.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the claims
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the rent table of the book: the amount paid for x chairs and y tables, with the amount returned taken away in a bracket

marks.shop: the chair and table rent table appears
marks.back: the amount returned appears inside a bracket with a minus sign before it
marks.flip: the signs inside the bracket flip

narration: <bookmark mark='shop'/>In your book, a shop rents out chairs and tables. The shop gives some rupees back when the furniture is returned.
<bookmark mark='back'/>The returned money is taken away from all that was paid. It sits in a bracket with the minus sign before it.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>That minus sign acts on every term inside the bracket.
